provenance: An entry belongs to B only if it appears in B's named sources: tool check lists (Schemathesis, RESTler), Segura et al.'s metamorphic output patterns, RFC 9110 (D3.1, D34).

entries.name: Server-error robustness
entries.probe: Send well-formed but unusual requests: optional parameters left out, boundary values, unexpected but valid combinations.
entries.oracle: The status is never 5xx; when the request is refused (4xx), the body carries an error message.

adherence.probe: At least one request uses unusual but well-formed input.
adherence.oracle: An assertion excludes 5xx, and a refusal is checked for an error message.

entries.name: Invalid input is rejected
entries.applicability: The operation takes parameters or a request body.
entries.probe: Break one documented constraint at a time: wrong type, key absent, value empty, value null, out of range, value outside the enum.
entries.oracle: The status is 4xx (not 2xx, not 5xx) and the body carries an error message.
entries.example: POST /books with {"title": null} → status in [400, 422]; body $.message exists.
entries.source: Schemathesis negative_data_rejection; Vieira et al. (DSN 2007) mutation operators by data type

adherence.probe: A request violates one documented input constraint.
adherence.oracle: An assertion expects a 4xx status, and the error body is checked.

entries.name: Valid input is accepted
entries.applicability: The operation takes parameters or a request body.
entries.probe: Send a request that meets every documented constraint: once with only required fields, once with optional fields as well.
entries.oracle: The status is 2xx and the response matches the documented schema.
entries.example: POST /books with {"title": "Emma", "year": 1815} → status in [200, 201]; responseSchema conformsToSpec.

adherence.probe: A request satisfies all documented constraints.
adherence.oracle: An assertion expects 2xx and checks the response against the schema or its fields.

entries.name: Response conformance
entries.applicability: A success response schema is documented.
entries.probe: Call the operation exactly as documented, with valid values for every parameter.
entries.oracle: The status is one of the documented codes and the body conforms to the documented schema (types, required fields).
entries.example: GET /books/{bookId} → status equals 200; responseSchema conformsToSpec; $.title isType string.

adherence.probe: The operation is called with valid, documented input.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks schema conformance or the type of documented fields.

entries.name: Invalid or unknown identifier
entries.applicability: The path contains an identifier parameter.
entries.probe: Use an identifier that does not exist, a malformed one (wrong type or format), or one of a deleted resource.
entries.oracle: The status is 404 (or 400 for a malformed value), never 2xx with data or 5xx; the body carries an error message.

adherence.probe: A request uses a non-existent or malformed identifier.
adherence.oracle: An assertion expects 404/400, and the error body is checked.

entries.name: Deleted resource is gone
entries.applicability: DELETE and GET exist for the same item.
entries.probe: Create or pick a resource, delete it, then read it again with the same identifier.
entries.oracle: The delete succeeds (2xx) and the follow-up read returns 404 with an error message.
entries.example: DELETE /books/{bookId} → status in [200, 204]; GET /books/{bookId} → status equals 404; $.message exists.

adherence.probe: A delete is followed by a read of the same identifier.
adherence.oracle: An assertion expects the read to fail with 404, and the body is checked.

entries.name: Created resource is available
entries.applicability: POST on a collection and GET on its items.
entries.probe: Create a resource, save its identifier with extract, then read it back by that identifier.
entries.oracle: The read returns 200 and shows the created resource; its identifier equals the saved one.
entries.example: POST /books → extract bookId from $.id; GET /books/{bookId} → status equals 200; $.id equals ${bookId}.

adherence.probe: A create is followed by a read of the new identifier.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks that the read-back resource carries the created identifier.

entries.name: Access control is enforced
entries.probe: Send the request with no credentials (auth none), and, if a second user exists, as that user.
entries.oracle: The status is 401 or 403 and the body contains no resource data.
entries.example: GET /books/{bookId} with auth none → status in [401, 403]; $.title notExists.
entries.source: Schemathesis ignored_auth; RESTler namespace rule checker

adherence.probe: A request is sent without credentials or as another user.
adherence.oracle: Assertions expect 401/403 and that no resource field is returned.

entries.name: Method semantics
entries.applicability: A GET, HEAD, PUT or DELETE operation.
entries.probe: Repeat a safe or idempotent request: GET twice, the same PUT twice, DELETE twice, and read the state after each.
entries.oracle: GET leaves state unchanged; a repeated PUT gives the same final state; a second DELETE never revives the resource or returns 5xx.

adherence.probe: The same safe or idempotent request is repeated.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks the state after the repetition.

entries.name: Equivalent requests agree
entries.applicability: A GET with two or more query parameters.
entries.probe: Send the same query twice with the parameters in a different order or in an equivalent form, saving a value from each.
entries.oracle: Both responses contain the same items, in any order: same length and the same identifiers.
entries.example: GET /books?genre=sf&year=1965 and GET /books?year=1965&genre=sf → compare the saved $[0].id values.
entries.source: Segura et al. (TSE 2018) metamorphic output pattern Equivalence

adherence.probe: Two equivalent forms of the same query are sent.
adherence.oracle: An assertion compares results of the two requests.

entries.name: Equal ordered results
entries.applicability: A GET with pagination parameters (limit, offset, page, per_page).
entries.probe: Request page 1 and page 2, then one larger page that covers both.
entries.oracle: Items keep their order: the large page equals the two pages joined; no item repeats across pages.
entries.example: GET /books?limit=2&page=2 → save $[0].id; GET /books?limit=4&page=1 → compare $[2].id with it.
entries.source: Segura et al. (TSE 2018) metamorphic output pattern Equality

adherence.oracle: An assertion compares items or order across the pages.

entries.name: Filtered result is a subset
entries.applicability: A GET with a filter or search parameter.
entries.probe: Request the unfiltered list, then the same list with a restrictive filter.
entries.oracle: Every filtered item satisfies the filter, and the filtered list is no longer than the unfiltered one.
entries.source: Segura et al. (TSE 2018) metamorphic output pattern Subset

adherence.probe: A filtered request is compared with or follows an unfiltered one.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks that the items satisfy the filter.

entries.name: Disjoint partitions
entries.applicability: A GET with a filter or an enumerated query parameter.
entries.probe: Request two disjoint partitions: two different enum values or two mutually exclusive filters.
entries.oracle: No item appears in both results; each result contains only items of its own partition.
entries.source: Segura et al. (TSE 2018) metamorphic output pattern Disjoint

entries.name: Partitions are complete
entries.applicability: A GET with a filter or an enumerated query parameter.
entries.probe: Request every partition (each enum value) and the unpartitioned list.
entries.oracle: The partitions together hold exactly the items of the unpartitioned list; their sizes add up.
entries.example: GET /books?status=lent, ?status=free and GET /books → $ lengthEquals the sum of the two partition lengths.
entries.source: Segura et al. (TSE 2018) metamorphic output pattern Complete

adherence.probe: All partitions and the full list are requested.
adherence.oracle: An assertion relates partition contents or sizes to the full list.

entries.name: Expected differences only
entries.applicability: A GET with field selection, sort or order parameters.
entries.probe: Request the same list with and without the projection or sort.
entries.oracle: Results differ only as expected: projected items carry only the requested fields; sorted items follow the sort key.
entries.source: Segura et al. (TSE 2018) metamorphic output pattern Difference

adherence.probe: A projected or sorted request is sent.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks the projected fields or the order.
